date_range.basis: Latest arXiv announcement batch; selected submissions carry UTC timestamps from 2026-10-26 through 2026-10-27.

title: arXiv Trending Biology and Biomedicine — Daily, 2026-10-28
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart and biomedical coverage is incomplete; this inferred, relevance-ranked selection is not a popularity ranking and does not represent bioRxiv, medRxiv, clinical practice, or biomedical research as a whole.

sections.title: Headline
sections.content: The Wednesday, 28 October 2026 announcement batch yielded 12 notable papers across biomolecules, genomics, quantitative biology, and medical physics. The strongest cluster is computational modeling tested against structural or cohort-scale data, with protein–glycan modeling, biomolecular dynamics, and synthetic genomics especially visible. arXiv has no official trending chart; the ranking is inferred from relevance and reported validation because attention evidence is sparse, and biomedical coverage is incomplete.

sections.title: Accurate structural modelling of protein-glycan recognition with GlycoWeave
sections.abstract: GlycoWeave uses chemically constrained diffusion and multiscale molecular representations to predict protein-bound glycan conformations, reporting a 71.9% Top-25 high-quality success rate on 698 complexes versus 19.2% for AlphaFold 3.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors claim internal-coordinate diffusion preserves glycan connectivity and stereochemistry while combining atom- and monosaccharide-level context; the abstract reports 0.34 seconds per sampled pose.
sections.unique_caveat: Structural-prediction benchmarking, not prospective binding or biochemical validation; training supervision also includes computationally refined structures.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Direct biomolecular focus; author-reported 698-complex benchmark with AlphaFold 3 comparison; Semantic Scholar citationCount 0 and influentialCitationCount 0 at snapshot.

sections.title: A unified coarse-grained neural network potential for the dynamics of biomolecular complexes
sections.abstract: AMARO v2.0 is a heavy-atom coarse-grained neural potential for proteins, drug-like molecules, and their complexes, evaluated across 262 complexes and selected binding case studies.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report charge-conditioned dynamics that distinguish trypsin–benzamidine protonation states and reach its crystal pose in 3.3 times as many trajectories as the tested all-atom baseline at fixed estimated GPU time.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors report over-favorable binding-free-energy estimates and remaining pose-recovery or site-specificity issues for SHP2 and CDK8; evidence is simulation, not experimental drug validation.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Direct biomolecular relevance; reported 262 complexes across 11 targets and comparisons with all-atom molecular mechanics; Semantic Scholar citationCount 0 and influentialCitationCount 0 at snapshot.

sections.title: HELICS: Biobank-scale Conditional Synthetic Genome Generation via Latent Flow Matching
sections.abstract: HELICS generates conditional synthetic common-variant genomes using latent flow matching trained on more than 417,000 UK Biobank genomes, with reported external allele-frequency and linkage-structure fidelity.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors claim phasing-free generation across more than 600,000 SNPs and show conditional dosage shifts correlated with published association weights.
sections.unique_caveat: The paper reports weaker fidelity for low-frequency variants and underrepresented ancestry groups; its principal benchmark focuses on common variants and European-ancestry evaluations.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Direct genomic-method contribution, biobank-scale training, external-cohort evaluation; arXiv comment lists NeurIPS 2026; Semantic Scholar citationCount 0 and influentialCitationCount 0 at snapshot.

sections.title: Retrospective macromolecular pool fraction mapping from conventional clinical MRI: a physics-guided self-supervised deep learning framework
sections.abstract: A physics-guided model estimates macromolecular pool fraction from conventional brain MRI and is evaluated on a multisite, multivendor dataset of 7,705 sessions, including 1,237 test sessions.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report stable MPF estimates across vendor/protocol groups and lower MPF in lesions than normal-appearing white matter in 70 disease-labeled sessions.
sections.unique_caveat: Retrospective estimates without paired quantitative reference scans; lesion association does not establish diagnostic performance or clinical utility.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Broad retrospective dataset and multisite/protocol consistency evaluation relevant to demyelinating disease; Semantic Scholar citationCount 0 and influentialCitationCount 0 at snapshot.

sections.title: pyTransRate: 1 reference-free quality assessment of de novo transcriptome assemblies with current aligners and quantifiers
sections.abstract: pyTransRate reimplements reference-free transcriptome-assembly quality scoring in Python and compares it with the prior TransRate release across 129 public assemblies.
sections.claimed_contribution: The author claims the updated Python implementation reproduces sequence metrics and read counts while supporting current aligners and compressed inputs.
sections.unique_caveat: Requires reads used to build each assembly, and its read-based scores are explicitly not numerically interchangeable with the old release.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Practical RNA-sequencing workflow relevance; 5,031 paired comparisons across 129 public assemblies and strong reported rank correlations; Semantic Scholar citationCount 0 and influentialCitationCount 0 at snapshot.

sections.title: Structure, Not Sequence: Tracking and Validating Folding Mechanisms in ESMFold's Trunk with Sparse Autoencoders
sections.abstract: Sparse autoencoders and attribution analyses are used to interpret ESMFold's internal folding computations and relate learned features to structural geometry and fold-quality predictions.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors claim sparse dictionaries separate inherited sequence semantics from pairwise geometric computation and that feature activations forecast ESMFold's own fold quality.
sections.unique_caveat: Computational analyses of one model; they do not independently establish that inferred circuits are causally necessary or generalize to other folding systems.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Direct protein-folding relevance and analysis connecting internal features to known biochemical structure; Semantic Scholar citationCount 0 and influentialCitationCount 0 at snapshot.

sections.title: Enhancing Clinical Classifier Robustness with Deep Representation Learning Based OOD Detection on DNA Methylation Data
sections.abstract: The authors test out-of-distribution detection for DNA-methylation tumor classifiers on public sarcoma and brain-tumor cohorts and an independent clinical dataset.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that 1D-SSA led their evaluated OOD methods, with mean AUROC 0.976 on the independent clinical test set.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract does not specify the clinical test-set size or composition; the study evaluates classifier quality control rather than prospective diagnostic outcomes.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Relevant genomic quality-control problem, multiple OOD methods, and independent clinical test set reported; Semantic Scholar citationCount 0 and influentialCitationCount 0 at snapshot.

sections.title: ACOR: incremental evidence accumulation towards real-time DNA storage reconstruction
sections.abstract: ACOR incrementally reconstructs DNA-storage sequences from streaming reads, with tests on simulated/public data and the authors' short-read wet-lab library.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors claim second-scale reconstruction and parallel speedups from tens to over a thousand-fold over the tested serial configurations.
sections.unique_caveat: Evidence concerns data-storage reconstruction on the tested libraries and baselines; no end-to-end production sequencing deployment is demonstrated.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Direct DNA-sequencing application and reported wet-lab-library evaluation over more than ten million reads; Semantic Scholar citationCount 0 and influentialCitationCount 0 at snapshot.

sections.title: HGPRGDel: GPR-Aware Learning and Ranking for Growth-Coupled Gene Deletion Design
sections.abstract: HGPRGDel learns gene-deletion priorities for microbial production and evaluates candidate strategies with constraint-based models across three metabolic reconstructions.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors claim explicit gene–protein–reaction logic improves intervention ranking while retaining downstream mechanistic assessment.
sections.unique_caveat: Computational reconstructions and reference-strategy recovery results, not experimentally measured strain yields or wet-lab confirmation.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Direct metabolic-engineering application, three model backgrounds, and reported recovery of 90% of reference deletion genes while examining fewer genes; Semantic Scholar citationCount 0 and influentialCitationCount 0 at snapshot.

sections.title: OpenGray: a benchmark for evaluating the decisions of radiotherapy planning agents
sections.abstract: OpenGray benchmarks whether radiotherapy-planning agents recognize incompatible dose goals and feasible plans, using 30 patients plus logs from 39 stereotactic radiosurgery runs.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that agents often failed to escalate contradictory plans despite high overall accuracy, motivating decision-centered evaluation.
sections.unique_caveat: The task set is small and partly constructed; observed agent behavior does not establish safety or performance in prospective clinical workflow.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Direct medical-physics application and reported decision errors hidden by aggregate accuracy; Semantic Scholar citationCount 0 and influentialCitationCount 0 at snapshot.

sections.title: Image-Domain CT Metal Artifact Reduction Using an Endpoint-Conditioned Diffusion Bridge
sections.abstract: RDBM-MAR uses an endpoint-conditioned diffusion bridge to reduce metal artifacts in CT and is tested on 14,000 paired challenge slices and one qualitative clinical case.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report improved PSNR, SSIM, and MAE using 10 deterministic reverse steps, while another comparator had the best LPIPS.
sections.unique_caveat: Quantitative test is on challenge slices and clinical evidence is one qualitative case; image metrics alone do not establish improved patient outcomes.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Medical-imaging method with a held-out test set and five named comparators; the authors report significant gains on three image metrics; Semantic Scholar citationCount 0 and influentialCitationCount 0 at snapshot.

sections.title: Optimization of 99mTc proton-induced production by means of cross-section measurements of technetium radioisotopes from molybdenum targets
sections.abstract: The authors measure proton-induced technetium production cross-sections on molybdenum targets and report production tests supporting a proposed medical-cyclotron route to 99mTc.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors identify approximately 16 MeV protons and a 0.5 mm enriched 100Mo target as suitable and calculate a yield near 1.7 GBq/μA for 10 hours of irradiation.
sections.unique_caveat: Reported yield is calculated from measured parameters; this does not establish routine-scale supply, cost, or clinical deployment.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Direct medical-isotope production relevance and measured reaction cross-sections followed by reported production tests; Semantic Scholar citationCount 0 and influentialCitationCount 0 at snapshot.

sections.title: Trending Research Themes
sections.content: Two papers address computational structure modeling with richer chemistry: GlycoWeave for glycan flexibility and stereochemistry, and AMARO v2.0 for charged biomolecular complexes. This is a small batch-level cluster, not evidence of a field-wide shift. Genomic data methods include HELICS, pyTransRate, ESMFold internal analysis, and ACOR DNA-sequencing reconstruction. Medical applications emphasize measurement and decision quality through MPF, methylation OOD detection, OpenGray, and CT-MAR. HGPRGDel and the 99mTc work are separate metabolic-design and isotope-production contributions.

sections.title: Open Problems and Research Directions
sections.content: Author-stated boundaries include AMARO's over-favorable free-energy estimates and pose/site-specificity failures, and HELICS's weaker low-frequency-variant and underrepresented-ancestry performance. Follow-ups include blinded glycan-complex tests plus structural or binding assays; calibration of AMARO against independently measured affinities and off-site binding; multi-ancestry external HELICS evaluation, especially rare variants, and tests of downstream association bias; a blinded multisite MPF comparison against quantitative magnetization-transfer scans and pathology-linked outcomes; and reporting size/composition and prospective referral consequences for DNA-methylation OOD cohorts. These are research proposals, not clinical advice.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.content: The batch emphasizes methods making molecular and clinical data more usable, but the strongest claims remain benchmark, retrospective, or computational results. Protein modeling and synthetic-genome generation show substantial reported evaluation; none establishes clinical benefit. Sparse attention evidence means the ordering reflects relevance and reported validation, not measured popularity.
